notes: Intent rules for the group acquisition flow.
Patterns are ordinary Python regular expressions and are matched against
NORMALISED text (see app/intent.py). Write them in normal Persian: the
engine runs the same character unification over the patterns, so you do
not have to think about Arabic yeh/kaf, ZWNJ or Persian digits here.
Use \s* between the words of a phrase so one pattern covers 'فیلترشکن',
'فیلتر شکن' and 'فیلتر  شکن'. Whitespace is already collapsed to single
spaces before matching.
The engine folds Arabic/Persian letter forms and digits in the patterns
too, and that includes punctuation: a Persian question mark becomes '?',
so a pattern that wants a literal question mark must escape it as \?.
How a message is judged:
* topic + at least one of (request, problem, poor_internet)  -> intent
* any standalone pattern                                     -> intent
* any ignore pattern                                         -> never
A bare mention of a VPN with no request and no complaint is NOT intent,
which is what keeps ordinary chatter in the group from triggering.
To extend: add patterns to a group. To add a new kind of supporting
signal, add a group under 'groups' with weight 1 and list its name in
'support_groups'. To change the balance, change 'topic_groups'.

topic.comment: Signals that the message is about circumvention. Alone they prove nothing.

request.comment: Signals that the user wants something. Supporting signal only.

problem.comment: Signals that something is broken. Supporting signal only.

comment: Complaints about connectivity in general. On their own they are NOT
enough — half the group complains about slow internet — so they only
count when the message is also about circumvention.
Phrases that are unambiguous on their own: someone asking how to get
past a block without naming a tool. Keep this list tight — every entry
Hard vetoes, checked first. A competing seller advertising in the group
is not a customer, and answering them with a trial link is noise.
